hook: Tripathi has spent his career on the unglamorous but consequential work of making health data actually move between systems, first from the policy side as the U.S. government's top health IT official, and now from inside a leading hospital system, applying that same interoperability and governance discipline to how AI gets deployed in clinical care.
name: Micky Tripathi

quote.text: Trust in AI in health care will be earned through transparency, not assumed through technology.
quote.context: A recurring theme in Tripathi's public remarks and ONC policy statements on health AI transparency, 2023-2024

moniker: Federal Architect of Health AI Policy

reading.body:
Micky Tripathi's most consequential contribution to health AI is the HTI-1 rule, the first federal mandate requiring transparency disclosures for predictive algorithms embedded in certified electronic health record systems, finalized under his leadership at ONC in 2024.

The pattern across his career is consistent: Tripathi has worked on the infrastructure layer beneath AI and clinical data, not the algorithms themselves. Regional health information exchange in Massachusetts, national interoperability standards at ONC, and now AI governance at Mayo Clinic all address the same problem, which is that data and models are only as useful as the systems that move, govern, and disclose them reliably. The HTI-1 rule is significant because it attaches transparency requirements to certification, meaning health IT vendors seeking federal certification must meet disclosure standards for clinical AI, not as a voluntary commitment but as a condition of market participation.

The data covers his policy and governance roles but does not address the technical content of the algorithms he has overseen, the clinical outcomes of systems he has governed, or the enforcement record of HTI-1 since finalization. His move from ONC to Mayo Clinic in 2024 is a single data point, not a trend, so no broader claim about federal-to-health-system talent flows is supported here.

Led federal rulemaking on health data interoperability and AI transparency in certified health IT
Now Chief Artificial Intelligence Implementation Officer at Mayo Clinic
Previously led the Massachusetts eHealth Collaborative and CRICO
